why: Same notions (constant sc-structure on the target, f ∘ E.toBase l on U_l, Mathlib ContDiffOn, IsSck), so A ⇒ B is corollary_1_2_5_text with V = Fin N → ℝ on the sc-domain U. B ⇒ A fails for a genuine reason: every conjunct of A is stated for an arbitrary IsScDomain U (e.g. a closed disc, not relatively open in a partial quadrant), while B covers only relatively open subsets of partial quadrants. A's other generalization, an arbitrary finite-dimensional normed target V instead of Fin N → ℝ with the sup norm, is only effort: on relatively open subsets of partial quadrants all six conjuncts follow from B (B_general transports along a linear isomorphism ℝᴺ ≅ V via the induced sc-operator between constant sc-structures and the chain rule IsSck.comp; B_to_A_quadrant then derives the strong-hypothesis, base-level, k = 0 and sc-smooth variants; rt_check OK). So the only genuine gap is the domain class.
overlap: n/a (B_to_A not proved); B_general uses IsSck.comp, IsSck.congr, ScOperator.isScSmooth and isScDomain_univ (which go through proposition_1_2_4, not an item theorem), no banned theorem.
